implementation_notes: Modern default: register the shared security sequence as filters - a global or per-controller IAsyncAuthorizationFilter alongside [Authorize] policies - so the MVC action invocation pipeline runs it before the action and short-circuits by setting context.Result. The framework owns the pipeline and the ordering, the base controller hook is not needed for the standard checks, and middleware covers endpoint-routed and non-MVC paths. Use the base-controller hook only for shared steps outside the authorization model.
pitfalls: Global filters surround controller filters and the after-code runs in reverse order; do not rely on attribute order alone to express the security sequence.
An authorization filter must assign context.Result to short-circuit; throwing produces a different response contract than returning a result.
Filters and middleware are different pipelines: a check placed in middleware sees the request before routing and cannot use action metadata.

variants.name: Shared base controller with an OnActionExecuting template hook
variants.implementation_notes: The classic MVC form: every controller derives from one project base controller whose OnActionExecuting override runs the shared sequence (session validation, tenant resolution, audit stamping) before the action method, and whose OnActionExecuted records the outcome. It is the literal base-action structure and remains useful for shared steps that are not authorization decisions, or when the checks must be independent of the authorization policy system.
pitfalls: Razor Page handler methods cannot take action filters, so the hook does not cover them; apply the checks to the PageModel instead.
OnActionExecuting runs after authorization filters have already decided; do not place a decision that must gate the action inside it.
